study_identification_part.si4_title: Molecular and micro-architectural mapping of gray matter alterations in psychosis

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Characterize molecular and micro-architectural attributes that underlie cortical volume deviations across psychosis-related groups using centile-based normative modeling; map deviations to 46 neurobiological features to test regional vulnerability hypotheses.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (FDR-corrected) for global/group centile differences; region-wise Cohen's d maps for between-group effect sizes with permutation tests and FDR; multivariate PCA-CCA linking regional centiles (and effect sizes) to 46 neurobiological features, with PLS used to confirm results; spatial spin tests to account for spatial autocorrelation.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: All psychosis-related groups show reduced cortical GM centiles below normative trajectories, strongest and most widespread in FEP and chronic SCZ/SAD; neurobiological features, especially metabolism and neurotransmitter receptors, co-localize with regions showing greatest deviations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Centiles were computed for 38,696 HC and 1,256 individuals across eight diagnoses grouped into SCZ/SAD-relatives, PE, FEP, and SCZ/SAD-chronic. Global GM centiles were significantly reduced in all groups (Wilcoxon FDR: relatives P=0.0021; PE P=0.0124; FEP P<1e-7; chronic P<1e-28). FEP and SCZ showed widespread regional reductions, SAD showed reductions in most regions, and PE-clinical showed 11 reduced regions; PE-suspected and PE-definite did not differ from HC. Neurobiological similarity correlated with structural co-vulnerability across groups (Pearson r=0.21, P_spin<1e-6), indicating that regions sharing neurobiological profiles tend to exhibit similar vulnerability patterns.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Global centile correction analyses performed; Euler number (image quality) assessed; full analysis code and dataset access links provided (GitHub).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Heterogeneous groups and varying sample sizes; potential medication effects in chronic patients; normative models available only for hemispherically averaged cortical volumes (34 DK regions); risk of CCA overfitting mitigated via PCA first and PLS confirmation; neurobiological data derived from healthy individuals; reported loadings instead of weights though both were similar.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Centiles derived from BrainChart models span 17 post-conception weeks to 100 years (per Discussion), enabling lifespan-standardized centiles. Due to model availability, only 34 DK regions (hemisphere-averaged) were used. Healthy controls included across clinical datasets total n=38,232 for the chronic group datasets; additional HC cohorts for FEP (n=195) and ALSPAC (n=269) are listed in Subjects. Data availability and code links are provided in the article (e.g., GitHub: RafaelRomeroGarcia/NeurobiologyCentilesPsychosis).
